name: build-vs-adopt
description: Compare custom implementation with existing libraries, services, and project capabilities; use when selecting an approach for a new capability or integration.

# Build versus adopt

Clarify the user need, constraints, and success criteria before selecting an approach.

- Inspect current project capabilities and established dependencies first.
- Compare adopting, extending, building, and deferring. Include fit, maintenance, lifecycle, security/privacy, licensing, operability, and total complexity.
- Verify candidate claims from current official documentation and repository evidence; distinguish fact from estimate.
- Prefer an existing fit when it meets requirements. Build when the need is distinctive or existing options fail important constraints.
- Where an adopted dependency may change, use an interface only when replaceability is a real requirement and the abstraction is proportionate.
- Recommend one option, explain tradeoffs and migration/exit costs, and propose focused validation.

Do not add dependencies or implement a choice without task approval.
